contract.why_single_layer: route_maze_batch.DRU_CLASS: on ONE routable layer the maze cannot express a barrel at all, so the .kicad_dru 'USB pair is forbidden on In2' rule becomes a shape the router cannot draw rather than a rule it may break.

free_space_corridor.method: BFS over maze3d.Field.blk on F.Cu at a 0.05 mm lattice between the free cells within 2.5 mm of each terminal group -- the same blocked grid route_join searches, so a corridor this says is absent is one the router cannot find either.

J3->U10.note: greedy, NOT minimal -- blocked_along ties at 182 cells throughout, so the ranking carried no information and the order is effectively alphabetical
J3->U10.verdict: RECOVERABLE -- a 3.51 mm free path for a 7.3 mm direct leg

R33/34->U1.verdict: NOT RECOVERABLE AS A LANE -- 76.80 mm of free path for a 21.9/24.3 mm direct leg is a 3.2-3.5x detour against a 25 mm diff_pair_uncoupled budget.  Opening the corridor is not the same as having one.

next_capabilities_named.name: corridor reservation honoured by the router
next_capabilities_named.shape: maze3d.Field already takes `guard={layer: [(x, y, keepout_nm), ...]}` and route_maze_batch already has --guard.  A corridor is the same object as a pour-bond tube: points with a keep-out radius.  What is missing is (a) an emitter that samples a reserved centreline and (b) an `exempt` list on a guard record, since guard_for only exempts the single net named on the record and a corridor must exempt a whole netclass.
next_capabilities_named.why: stop the bleeding before recovering anything; a corridor recovered and not reserved is lost again by the next batch

next_capabilities_named.name: differential-PAIR proposer
next_capabilities_named.second_customer: /04_SPI_B_RADIOS_NFC/NFC_RFI1 and NFC_RFI2, the two nets route_maze_batch.EXCLUDE holds out for length/symmetry
next_capabilities_named.why: a per-net maze cannot hold diff_pair_gap or a diff_pair_uncoupled budget; the first F/B screen was refused by KiCad for exactly that, at 36.653 mm for an 8.465 mm leg.  A fat-centreline wavefront at 2*W + gap = 0.70 mm, split into two tracks offset by +/-0.225 mm, meets the gap by construction and leaves only the fanout uncoupled.

not_done_and_why: The In2 through-via ruling was NOT taken.  It would have been the cheap answer -- .kicad_dru 'USB pair is forbidden on In2' disallows `via` as well as `track`, and on a 6-layer board that forbids EVERY through barrel, which over-reaches the rule's own title ('it has no business leaving F.Cu').  It is not taken because it buys NOTHING at this geometry: with F+B already permitted -- vias and all -- MCU_N is NO_PATH and MCU_P needs 30.766 mm and four barrels.  Relaxing a rule that is not the binding constraint would spend real safety margin for no connection.
note: READ-ONLY measurement of the USB 2.0 link on the authoritative board. USB-C data/programming is a Demo MUST-HAVE feature and 'USB differential routing and constraints complete' is an explicit release gate, so its four open edges are scope-critical rather than ordinary.  Everything below is measured; nothing is inferred from the earlier contract note, which is shown to be STALE.

q2w_whole_net_single.result: NO OPENER on either connector edge

regression_since_the_contract_note.conclusion: THE RESERVED CORRIDOR IS BEING CONSUMED.  .kicad_dru section 6 reserves F.Cu over In1 for this pair in words, and nothing in the tool chain enforces that reservation on a router, so every whole-board maze batch since has been free to lay copper in it -- and has.  44 foreign F.Cu nets now carry copper inside the USB window.  This is a FABRICATION-CRITICAL trend, not a static wall.

usb_family_eviction.conclusion: THE WALL IS NOT USB-INTERNAL.  Evicting every USB net board-wide changes nothing about the two hauls.
